name: Matt Barr
fact: Flag for the editor, not a fix: the worklist carries Matt Barr (2018-19 to 2020-21) and Matthew Barr (2017-18) as two people, and they are very probably one. The Herald of 13 March 2019 names "Campus Improvements Committee Chair Matt Barr" as a co-author of the office-hours amendment, alongside Director of Public Relations Noah Moore and Public Relations Committee Chair Ashlynn Evans. WKU's alumni site lists "Matthew ('21) and Ashlynn (Evans) Barr ('21)" as a married couple, which places a Matthew Barr in the same SGA cohort as Ashlynn Evans and graduating in 2021, consistent with a single unbroken run 2017-18 to 2020-21.

src.label: College Heights Herald, "SGA passes bill to amend constitution", 13 Mar 2019

name: Noah Moore
fact: Caution for anyone hunting this face: there are two Noah Moores at WKU in these years and they are not the same man. The SGA one was elected a junior senator in April 2018 and was Director of Public Relations by March 2019. The other, Noah Moore of Fort Thomas (netid noah_moore786), was a Public Relations, Spanish and Arabic triple major, class of 2021, a Herald features reporter, an admissions tour guide and a Sigma Phi Epsilon officer; WKU's 2020 write-up of his SigEp Tragos Quest award lists five campus offices he held and SGA is not among them, and he was a junior in 2019-20, when the SGA Moore was Secretary of the Senate. His studio portrait, captioned "Tour guide Noah Moore", is therefore not a portrait of the SGA officer and was not used.

src.label: WKU News, "WKU junior selected as 2020 SigEp Tragos Quest to Greece Scholar"

name: Aubrey Kelley
fact: The two WKU sources for the 2019-20 cabinet disagree about her office. The Herald's report of the first meeting of the year, 4 September 2019, lists the confirmations as "Aubrey Kelley, Chief of Staff, Ashlynn Evans, Chief of Public Relations, Abbey Norvell, Director of Academic and Student Affairs, Paul Brosky, Director of Information Technology". SGA's own surviving cabinet page for that year gives Will Harris as Chief of Staff and Aubrey Kelley as Director of Academic and Student Affairs.

src.label: WKU SGA, executive cabinet page for 2019-20 (wku.edu/sga/2018-2019-executive/officehours.php)

name: Lyndsey Kelley
fact: Her year as chief of staff did not run to its end. A Herald photograph of the SGA meeting of 13 February 2024 is captioned "Student Body President Sam Kurtz (left) and Chief of Staff Donte Reed (right)", so somebody else held the office by that February.

name: Shelby Robertson
fact: She was elected speaker of the senate at SGA's first official meeting of 2020-21, on 6 October 2020, beating Brenna Matthews after both candidates gave speeches; the senate voted by Google Form because the meeting ran in person and on Zoom at once. In October 2021, as a committee head, she was working on a proposal to fund a scholarship for rural students.

src.label: College Heights Herald, "SGA votes on budget at first official meeting of the year", 7 Oct 2020

name: Zachary Skillman
fact: He and his identical twin brother Jacob came to WKU together from Katy, Texas, both reading Business Economics with a Computer Information Systems minor, and both sat as senators-at-large. Their father took a WKU degree in 1994. WKU's feature on the pair carries the only photograph of them, and it is uncaptioned, so it cannot be used to tell one twin from the other.

src.label: WKU News, "Twin brothers take college journey together"

name: Kody Okert
fact: Outside SGA he ran the fraternity system: Interfraternity Council vice president of recruitment, then IFC president, and a member of Kappa Sigma. He helped plan WKU's Walk a Mile in Her Shoes event against sexual assault, and WKU's Greek community gave him the Charley Pride Spirit Award in 2021.

src.label: WKU CEBS News, "Fraternities seek to change culture through Walk a Mile event"

name: Ian Hamilton
fact: The Gordon Ford College of Business named him Outstanding Junior in Management and Information Systems at its recognition dinner. He is from Georgetown.

src.label: WKU Gordon Ford College of Business news, recognition dinner report

name: Abhishek Bose
fact: SGA's own executive cabinet page for 2016-17 is still live on wku.edu and lists the whole cabinet: Jay Todd Richey president, Kate Hart executive vice president, Hannah Neeper administrative vice president, James Line chief of staff, Josh Knight director of academic and student affairs, Abhishek Bose director of information technology, Murphy Burke director of public relations.

name: Parker Raybourne
fact: He graduated in 2022 in political science, public relations and advertising, and was awarded a Fulbright English Teaching Assistantship to Indonesia for 2023-24, WKU's fifth Fulbright grantee of that year. He had studied in twelve countries as an undergraduate and represented Potter College on the Dean's Council of Students.

src.label: WKU News, "Parker Raybourne '22 Awarded Fulbright US Student Grant"

name: Reed Breunig
fact: He was crowned WKU's 2022 Coming Home King on 19 February 2022, one of twenty-one candidates; he was sponsored by Phi Mu and read healthcare administration. He was also an admissions ambassador and a co-chair of Dance Big Red.

src.label: WKU News, "Reed Breunig crowned WKU's 2022 Coming Home King"

name: Meghan Pierce
fact: She read international affairs, Arabic and economics, came to WKU from the Gatton Academy having started Arabic to graduate from it with honours, won a Gilman scholarship to study in Amman, and held a Critical Language Scholarship for Arabic before being named an alternate for a second in 2024.

src.label: WKU Department of Modern Languages student profile, "Meghan Pierce, International Affairs and Arabic, Class of 2024"
